title: Repair: seven should-fix findings in the herdr executor, all 'an unknown answered as a fact'
description:
Seven should-fix findings from the Phase 2 final review (zus), all in the herdr
executor, all LATENT — usableProfile refuses any non-subprocess executor, so
nothing constructs herdr.Executor outside tests yet. Each cites the guarantee it
undermines.

1. reclaim.go:66-76 — survey() SWALLOWS the worktree.list error. Attribution
   then answers "gone", and dispose removes nothing while recording a successful
   teardown. That is 5hz's own orphan incident, reproduced in the code written
   to prevent it, with the doc claiming fail-closed. "herdr did not answer" is
   not evidence that nothing is there.

2. wall.go:52 — minStopProtocol is the client's PIN (20), not its FLOOR (19), so
   every bounded dispatch against a protocol-19 herdr the client otherwise
   supports is refused as unenforceable. jv7 separated floor from pin precisely
   so a supported-but-older server still works.

3. wall.go:139-153 — the wall marker and the words "the interrupt was delivered
   through herdr" are written even when herdr answered agent_not_found. An agent
   that exited on its own then collects as wall_clock_exceeded: a sentence about
   an event that did not happen, which is the x9x rule (claim only what you
   observed) broken in gwc's code.

4. inspect.go:139 — observe returns `succeeded` from the report BEFORE the
   pastWall branch, so an agent that reports and keeps running is never stopped,
   and dispose then refuses it as working, forever. This is the same
   report-outranks-liveness shape the local executor's Cancel was fixed for.

5. strict.go:266 — bcv's presence rules cover the agent liveness fields but NOT
   workspace_id, checkout_path or the worktree path — the fields 5hz's
   attribution is keyed on. A rename there silently answers "gone", which is the
   loud-not-silent guarantee bcv exists for, missing on the fields that decide a
   teardown.

6. record.go:147 — agentName truncates to 32 characters AFTER appending "-aN",
   so a long tick id drops the attempt suffix and two attempts of one tick share
   an agent name. Truncate the tick id, never the discriminator.

7. dispose.go:258 — !LaunchConfirmed short-circuits the liveness question
   entirely, on exactly the path where the launch outcome is UNKNOWN. Shares a
   root with tick 1eq's first blocker; if 1eq lands first, check whether this is
   already covered.

Do them as one pass — they are all the same family (an unknown answered as a
fact) — and say in the RESULT which of the epic's guarantees each restores.

acceptance_criteria: Each of the seven is fixed or explicitly declined with a reason: survey propagates the worktree.list error instead of answering gone; the wall-clock protocol check uses the client's floor rather than its pin; a wall marker is written only when the interrupt was actually delivered; a reporting-but-live agent is still stopped at its bound; the strict presence rules cover the fields attribution is keyed on; the agent name truncates the tick id rather than the attempt discriminator; and the unconfirmed-launch path asks about liveness rather than assuming. Tests cover the ones that change behaviour; make test-short green.
closed_reason: All seven should-fix items resolved: survey propagates the worktree.list error instead of answering gone; the wall-clock check uses the client's floor not its pin; a wall marker is written only when the interrupt was delivered; a reporting-but-live agent is still stopped at its bound; strict presence covers the fields attribution is keyed on; the agent name truncates the tick id rather than the attempt discriminator; and the unconfirmed-launch teardown asks about liveness. Gate green.
